content:
In the last couple of days, there have been two reports highlighting different ways in which Apple is looking to boost its earnings by increasing its services revenue.

In my view, Apple should absolutely adopt the first approach, but definitely not the second — and it looks like Phil Schiller may share this view too…

Let me first summarize these two reports.

Home Security & Monitoring Service

On Friday, Bloomberg reported that Apple may be planning to launch a brand new home security and monitoring service, complementing some of the new home hardware products we've been expecting.

Squeezing More From The App Store

The second report from the same source, published on Sunday, said the company is exploring ways to extract more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple Should NOT Do The Latter

Taking the two in reverse order, I think the second approach would be a very serious mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly position on iPhone app sales has come under attack from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an iPhone app, you have to do so through the official App Store, with no alternative at all, and you just have to accept the company's take-it-or-leave-it terms.

I know there's a common argument that nobody is forced to buy an iPhone, or to develop an app for it, but that's not how the most laissez-faire form of capitalism actually works: even in the US, where there have been antitrust laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, you become subject to behavioral constraints to ensure you don't abuse that position.

Trying to squeeze more money from the App Store is exactly the opposite of skating to where the puck is going — and reportedly Schiller agrees, with Bloomberg suggesting that's one of the reasons he's stepped back.

Innovative Services Is The Right Direction

By contrast, launching new innovative services that people want to buy is absolutely the right thing for Apple to do. I can easily see the value in the company offering a home security monitoring service.

As long ago as 2024, I argued that making its own smart home cameras would be one of the … smartest moves the company could make. I feel the same way about the rumored Apple smart doorbell. Adding an optional service bundle to security products makes complete sense for two reasons.

First, all the privacy arguments I've made before. HomeKit Secure Video already does great work in ensuring the privacy of security camera footage. If there's one company I'd trust to do AI analysis of security camera images, it's Apple.

Second, Apple is of course best placed to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit environment. I'm sure there are many other areas where Apple could offer similar benefits.

For me, the key is that Apple needs to treat services the same way it treats hardware. Create great products that people willingly and happily pay for; not extract money in annoying ways that leave customers, developers, and regulators alike unhappy.

What do you think? Please share your views in the comments.
